clue.text: Small parts in last days — four times out of twelve

definitions.meaning: fractions of one divided into thirty equal pieces are small parts

definitions.text: last days — four times out of twelve
definitions.meaning: April, June, September and November end on their thirtieth day, so four months in twelve have their last day on that date

explanation.surface: Someone describing tiny portions of the final days of something, with a puzzling statistic attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: four of the twelve months have thirty days, so their last day is the thirtieth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fractions with a denominator of thirty are tiny portions of a whole, hence small parts.

clue.text: College boy in complete agreement

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A student and his father see eye to eye on everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is a synonym for total accord, people acting or speaking together as one.

clue.text: Film — dry, about French street, not entirely grim

indicators.note: about says the dry letters surround the street and the trimmed word

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so abstaining from alcohol, dry
rue is French for street

indicators.note: not entirely says the final letter of grim is dropped

explanation.surface: A film critic sums up a picture: dry, with a Paris street scene, somewhat bleak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dry' means teetotal here, not arid; 'about' wraps those letters round the street, and 'not entirely' trims the last letter of grim.
explanation.definitionFit: True Grit is a western movie, filmed in 1969 with John Wayne and remade in 2010.

clue.text: PM in garden

definitions.meaning: Anthony ... was a British Prime Minister in the 1950s
the biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived was a garden

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister out among the flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are proper names: Sir Anthony, UK premier 1955-57, and the paradise garden of Genesis.

clue.text: Tears linen, playing old game

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of tears linen are played about with and reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone rips the tablecloth while engaged in some antique sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' looks like part of the game picture but signals the anagram of TEARS LINEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the original indoor racket sport, played since medieval times, so an old game.

clue.text: Cruel people using guns at first for time in European city

indicators.note: for says one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: brutes are savage, cruel people

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of guns is used

explanation.surface: Violent thugs with firearms terrorising a city somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the T (time) in BRUTES for G, the first letter of 'guns'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bruges is a medieval city in Belgium, famous for its canals.

clue.text: Referring to children as over- sentimental, keep complaining, ultimately horrible

parts.note: twee means sickly sweet, over-sentimental
to nag is to complain persistently

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of horrible

explanation.surface: A grumble about children being cloying, whiny and, in the end, dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweenage describes youngsters between childhood and teens, so it is an adjective relating to kids.

clue.text: Architect's songbird

definitions.meaning: Sir Christopher ... designed St Paul's Cathedral in London
a tiny brown bird with a loud song

explanation.surface: A building designer's pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the famous English architect is also the name of a small singing bird.

clue.text: Long struggle of batter: day runs were hard

indicators.note: to batter is to beat out of shape, so the letters of the following words are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cricket batsman's long innings, scoring slowly on a tough day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' reads as a cricket batsman, but it is the verb signalling the anagram of DAY RUNS WERE HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The conflict between England and France lasted over a century (1337-1453), a long struggle indeed.

clue.text: Girl got up about one

indicators.note: about says the getting-up word wraps around the numeral

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, so got up
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A girl rose at around one o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosie is a female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Colour of love, say? Certainly not poetic in retrospect

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, so nil
e.g. means for example, so say

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the poetic word is read backwards

parts.note: ne'er is the poetic form of never, certainly not

explanation.surface: Musing on what colour love might be, while denying it is poetic in hindsight.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green shade, named after the river.

clue.text: One racing off showing lack of knowledge

indicators.note: off suggests going wrong or out of place, so the letters of one racing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A competitor heading off at speed shows they don't know the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks like the start of a race but signals the anagram of ONE RACING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is precisely the state of not knowing, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Idea about new female in charge that's not fanciful?

indicators.note: about says the idea word wraps around the three abbreviations

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: A thought regarding a new woman taking over, offered as something down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works attributively, as in a nonfiction book: writing about real things, not imagined ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Factual writing deals with real events rather than invented stories, hence is not imaginative.

clue.text: Such a clue oddly established standard

indicators.note: oddly says to take the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A setter remarks that a clue like this one meets the accepted norm.
explanation.definitionFit: A scale is a fixed graded system for measuring, so a set benchmark.

clue.text: Travelling around, I represent business

indicators.note: travelling around suggests the letters of i represent wander into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A sales rep on the road speaks for their company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling around' fits the touring salesman picture but signals the anagram of I REPRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a commercial undertaking or company, a synonym for a business.

clue.text: Seeing nth bottle being ordered, economise?

indicators.note: being ordered suggests the letters of seeing nth bottle are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Watching yet another bottle being ordered at the bar, someone wonders about cutting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being ordered' reads as buying drinks but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cut spending, as one pulls a belt tighter when food is scarce.

clue.text: Give information about fight for outdoor container

parts.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone to the police
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: An informant reports on a brawl in search of an outdoor receptacle.
explanation.walkthrough: To grass, in British slang, is to tell the police about someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass box is the collecting bin on a lawnmower that catches the cut cuttings outside.

clue.text: Quiet worker in East End suspended silk fabric

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End drop their H's, so the opening letter of the word is lost

parts.note: hung means suspended

explanation.surface: A silent labourer in London's East End is hanging silk cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in East End' removes the H from HUNG, as a Cockney (East End Londoner) would.
explanation.definitionFit: Shantung is a raw silk cloth with a slubbed texture, originally from the Chinese province.

clue.text: Wanders off? Not right — remains

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is left out

parts.note: strays means wanders off

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone wandered off, then correcting: no, they stayed put.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to remain, so the third-person verb forms match as synonyms.

clue.text: Protective cover reduces heat haze to some extent …

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A protective covering cuts down shimmer from the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case, such as for a blade, so a protective covering.

clue.text: Entrant is processed immediately

indicators.note: processed suggests the letters of entrant is are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A newcomer's application is dealt with straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is an old legal word for at once, without delay.

clue.text: … and another one that's securing home?

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so that wraps around the home word

parts.note: taken as written
in means at home

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: here is a second protective cover, one guarding the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 20 down: 'another one' means another protective cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel military helmet is protective headgear, so another piece of protective covering.

clue.text: Looked up to revolutionary having absorbed short description (note)

indicators.note: having absorbed says the revolutionary word takes in the others

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
spec is short for specification, a description
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A radical who took in a brief description, plus a musical note, was admired.
explanation.definitionFit: Respected and admired both mean held in high esteem, the past tense matching the idiom.

clue.text: Study about Christian era

parts.note: re means about, concerning
AD, anno Domini, marks years of the Christian era

explanation.surface: Research into the period since Christ was born.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is to study it at university, a British usage.

clue.text: Twilight of the French Sun King

parts.note: du is French for of the
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: The fading glory of Louis XIV, France's Sun King.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun King was Louis XIV, which makes 'French' read as part of a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is the dim period after sunset, a synonym for evening twilight.

clue.text: Cosmetic from past one remembers

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A beauty product from long ago that someone recalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Toner is a skin lotion used to tighten pores, a cosmetic product.

clue.text: When best wear is continually needed?

definitions.text: When best wear is continually needed?

parts.words: When best wear is continually needed?
parts.note: Sunday best is one's finest clothing, so a long run of Sundays would need it constantly

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means a very long time; literally, a stretch made of Sundays would demand your Sunday best throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an extremely long time, and literally describes a period full of Sundays.
